text.p: Australian imports data for August will be released at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT) today.
The median forecast of the 28 economists Reuters surveyed is for a 2.2 percent rise in imports. Forecasts range from a 1.0 percent fall to a 5.0 percent rise.

Only three economists were expecting a fall in August, with most saying that after falling in the last three months, statistical volatility and the likely inclusion of an aircraft worth about A$100 million, and a softer Australian dollar in the month all pointing to a rise in the imports bill.
Recent months data, and August forecasts, are tabled below.
Imports (A$, million) Mar Apr May Jun Jul Aug(f)

Imports have fallen by a total of 8.0 percent over the last three months, and the weakest area has been capital goods. In the last two months, capital goods have fallen a huge 22.7 percent, weakness which sits at odds with bullish expectations for business investment in 1996/97, economists said.
Consumption goods, which have held up reasonably well in recent months, are expected to show some signs of softness.

With the strong July retail trade rise of 2.4 percent boosted by department store clearance sales, economists said stores may be running down stock levels, and so would not be importing new stock just yet.
With imports having weakened around the middle of the year, and the current account seemingly under control, economists said market attention had shifted away from the imports.
More attention was being paid to the labour force data given its direct influence on interest rates, but a strong imports number should still retain the capacity to surprise markets.
